L45@P1: strategies are very similar. First one treats projective spaces directly via a direct computation of
L46@P1: the cohomology of line bundles, then a dévissage is performed using Chow’s Lemma.
L47@P1: The main theorem of this article is that these GAGA results are true much more generally and
L48@P1: can be put into a single framework. Essentially all existing results follow very easily from ours
L49@P1: (see §9). We state one such result in the noetherian situation for locally ringed G-spaces.

L72@P1: In future work, we will apply it to algebraic stacks and their derived counterparts. Our approach
L73@P1: is related to the non-noetherian GAGA results in the Stacks Project [Stacks, Tag 0DIJ]. While
L74@P1: Theorem A (and B, below) is an immediate consequence of much more general results (Theorems
L75@P1: 6.1, 8.1, and 9.1), we give a simple and direct proof in §2.
L76@P1: Remark 1.1. Basic properties of noetherian local rings show that Theorem A(5) is implied by:
L77@P1: (5’) if x ∈ Xcl,c, then OX,x is noetherian and the morphism OX,c(x) → OX,x induces an isomorphism on maximal-adic completions.
L78@P1: Conditions (1) of (2) of Theorem A are typically established by theorems in analysis. For
L79@P1: example, in the archimedean case, they are Oka’s Theorem [Oka50] and Cartan–Serre’s finiteness
L80@P1: theorem [CS53]. In the non-archimedian case, it is Kiehl’s finiteness theorem [Kie67]. In the case
L81@P1: of formal schemes, it is Grothendieck’s finiteness theorem [EGA, III.3.4.2]. Note that there is no
L82@P1: circularity here: none of these results have anything to do with GAGA theorems or their proofs.
L83@P1: It is even possible to use the analytic finiteness results to prove the algebraic ones [Duc15]. The
L84@P1: recent work [Zav21] shows that the ideas in this article persist to almost mathematics. Theorem
L85@P1: A (and its generalizations considered in this paper) are currently not well-adapted to local or
L86@P1: henselian type analytifications (e.g., [AT19, Thm. C.1.1] or [Dev20]), however, as the boundedness
L87@P1: condition (2) is established via induction and GAGA.
L88@P1: Without finiteness results, however, we can establish the following.

L104@P2: Theorem B is sufficient to establish the full-faithfulness of the analytification of vector bundles
L105@P2: on the Fargues–Fontaine curve. Surprisingly, Theorem B is a consequence of a general Lefschetzstyle result (see §6), which establishes all existing full faithfulness results in the literature (see
L106@P2: §9).
L107@P2: In order to establish non-noetherian GAGA results in formal geometry (e.g., [FK18] or [Stacks,
L108@P2: Tag 0DIA]), the non-flatness of completions complicates matters significantly. These are dealt
L109@P2: with in §5. We work quite generally and expect these methods to be applicable to other types of
L110@P2: GAGA and Lefschetz-style results (e.g., in o-minimal geometry). In Appendix §A, we establish
L111@P2: functoriality results for the projection formula in symmetric monoidal categories, which turn out
L112@P2: to be critical for results like Theorem A.
